To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
agricultural intensification has already had, and is projected to have in the future, very serious detrimental impacts on the natural ecosystems of the planet.
agricultural intensification has had and will continue to have major detrimental impacts of global environmental quality.

the intensification of agriculture has been accompanied by large environmental impacts, that the projected intensification of agriculture in the future would have even larger environmental impacts, and that these impacts can be minimized by much more efficient use of agricultural nutrients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the environmental consequences of the intensification of global agricultural food production.
the impacts of agricultural intensification on the global environment and on ways to mitigate these detrimental effects.
the environmental impacts of agricultural intensification and the development of sustainable agricultural systems that minimize these impacts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the intensification of agriculture will have major negative impacts on the remaining natural ecosystems and their biodiversity, and that the impacts will be much greater than those associated with the recent doubling of global agricultural food production.

the recent intensification of global agriculture, and the anticipated intensification in the future, will have major and detrimental impacts on the remaining nonagricultural ecosystems of the world and their ability to provide essential ecosystem services to society.

the recent doubling of food production has been associated with major detrimental environmental impacts, and that future intensification of agriculture will have even more severe impacts unless more sustainable and efficient agricultural production practices are adopted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to develop more sustainable and efficient agricultural practices to minimize the negative environmental impacts of agriculture on the remaining natural ecosystems.
the world is in a very precarious position with respect to the sustainability of the agricultural system.
the global environmental impacts of agricultural intensification can be reduced only if the efficiency of nutrient use in agroecosytems is increased substantially.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the environmental impacts of agriculture are not only large and pervasive, they will become even more so in the future.

the environmental impacts of future intensification of global agriculture will be much greater than those of the last doubling, and will be difficult to mitigate unless the efficiency of nutrient use is increased substantially.
the intensification of agriculture has had and is continuing to have major impacts on nonagricultural ecosystems.
